themes.text: Attackers exploit a critical Cisco Expressway flaw and a China-linked group hit vCenter, JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard confirm vendor breaches, and DeepSeek raises $15.8 billion.
De'Longhi's La Marzocco division grows 35%, the ICO price edges down, and Kentucky launches a coffee science certificate.
Twenty-four teams form the Collective Cycling Group, TotalEnergies survives into 2027, and Garmin may share rider locations with Waze.
Experts say Thanksgiving flying is safe after the FAA meltdown, Expedia confirms a supply chain breach, and Black Friday hotel sales begin.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above the planned range
items.text: The price beat the marketed $70 to $78 range and Anthropic sold more shares than planned. Reports put the valuation near $1.5 trillion, though they differ on the total raised.

items.head: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon with a 1M-token context window
items.text: Priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, Neon scores 61 on the AA Intelligence Index and ranks first on AA's Coding Agent Index.

items.head: DeepSeek closes a $15.8 billion funding round
items.text: The roughly 105.5 billion yuan round brings DeepSeek's total funding to about $23.5 billion. Tencent and CATL tie as the largest investors at 9.5653% each.

items.head: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over chips reaching China
items.text: Rob Bonta's investigation covers whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors. CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.

items.head: Hackers exploit critical Cisco Expressway flaw to reach internal networks
items.text: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) gives unauthenticated attackers root. After a public exploit, attackers breached four devices, then went after SMB shares, SQL Server and GitLab credentials. Upgrade to X15.5.20 and check for compromise.

items.head: Chinese hackers exploited a critical vCenter flaw; Broadcom patches it now
items.text: CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) lets unauthenticated attackers take admin control of vCenter. A China-linked group used it since September. Broadcom lists no workaround, so patch to 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 or 8.0 U3m.

items.head: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm breaches at outside vendors
items.text: Attackers took marketing data that may include customer names and email addresses. All three say payment systems and card numbers were safe. The Russia-based extortion group n0n claimed the hacks.

items.head: Attackers exploit critical Apache Axis flaw to breach Confluence and Microsoft 365
items.text: CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8) in end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x was used against Confluence Data Center, with one attacker reaching Microsoft 365 within about 12 hours. CISA set a November 21 deadline.

items.head: PHP patches seven critical remote code execution flaws
items.text: PHP 8.6.0 and 8.5.13 fix all seven critical bugs, while 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 patch most issues. None of the new flaws is known to be exploited, but October's PHP2Shell bug is.

items.head: Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI hijacked to steal cloud credentials
items.text: Malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 use Python startup hooks to grab Azure, GitHub Actions, npm, Docker and Hugging Face secrets. Remove them and rotate any exposed credentials.

items.head: IEA: data centers to produce 70% more carbon emissions by 2030
items.text: An International Energy Agency report warns that emissions from data centers will climb as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth.

items.head: University of Michigan weighs a $785 million computing center with Los Alamos
items.text: Regents vote on a high-performance computing center on 144 acres in Ypsilanti Township, capped at 300,000 square feet and $785 million. The township opposes the project.

items.head: Google plans a $17 billion fuel-cell data center in Wyoming
items.text: Google's first Wyoming data center is a planned 702MW development powered by fuel cells with carbon capture and storage, and it uses air cooling, according to Mission Critical News.

items.head: Kraft Group proposes a $16 billion, 900MW campus in Massachusetts
items.text: The Kraft Group's Sutton, Massachusetts project would grow from two buildings to ten by 2033, reaching 900MW, Mission Critical News reports.

desks.title: Coffee
desks.blurb: What is moving the coffee business, and the shift from gas drum roasters to electric roasting.

sections.title: Industry and markets
sections.blurb: Prices, companies and rules that shape the cup.

items.head: De'Longhi revenue rises 7.7% as La Marzocco's division grows 35%
items.text: Third-quarter revenue reached €944.9 million and net income €84.5 million, up 19%. The professional division, home to La Marzocco and Eversys, grew more than 35%.

items.head: ICO coffee price edges down to $2.61 a pound in October
items.text: The ICO composite averaged $2.6126 per pound, down 0.3% from September. All three arabica groups rose, while robusta fell 2% to $1.6419.

items.head: University of Kentucky launches a coffee science certificate
items.text: The 12-credit undergraduate certificate in coffee science and culture opens for spring 2027, with core courses including Coffee Sensory Science plus two electives.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.head: Roastar packaging design awards
items.text: The third annual awards take up to three designs first printed by Roastar in 2026, plus a new tin-design contest for kids 13 and under. Winners come in early January.

items.head: NCA Convention, Austin, Texas
items.text: The National Coffee Association's annual convention comes to the JW Marriott Austin.

sections.title: Racing and rides
sections.blurb: The stories riders are talking about.

items.head: 24 teams form the Collective Cycling Group after One Cycling's collapse
items.text: The UK company, essentially One Cycling renamed, aims to market pro cycling's commercial rights. EF Education, Canyon-SRAM and Pinarello-Q36.5 confirmed; UAE and Red Bull are reportedly absent.

items.head: TotalEnergies team finds a three-year title sponsor to survive into 2027
items.text: The French team, which had about a week to find a sponsor before UCI 2027 registration, has reportedly secured three years of title funding, per Ouest France. It will get a new name and colours, with Pardus as bike sponsor.

items.head: Unconfirmed: Garmin may share riders' locations with Waze drivers
items.text: Code in Garmin Connect v5.31 hints at an opt-in 'Waze Location Sharing' feature that would use LiveTrack data to show drivers nearby cyclists. Neither Garmin nor Waze has announced it, and there's no timeline.

sections.title: Ride and race calendar
sections.blurb: US and world events coming up.

items.head: Turkey Roll Bicycle Rally, Denton, Texas
items.text: A Saturday bicycle rally in Denton on November 21, listed on NWCC's 2026 calendar of Texas bike rides. Check the organizer for routes and registration.

items.head: Texas MS 150: Houston and Austin to College Station
items.text: Two-day ride with starts in Houston and Austin, an overnight in La Grange and the finish in College Station.

items.head: Tour de France: Edinburgh to Paris
items.text: 21 stages and 3,479km, with time trials at Blois–Chambord and Toulouse and a Montmartre finale in Paris.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: After the FAA meltdown, experts say Thanksgiving flying is safe
items.text: A router swap reportedly set off the outage behind Friday's nationwide ground stop. Every plane landed safely, but understaffed controllers and old systems keep worries alive.

items.head: Expedia confirms breach through Qubole supply chain attack; hackers claim huge haul
items.text: Expedia told Skift that attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform. Wiz and Sentra link it to a stolen Qubole key. The extortion group n0n claims 830 million loyalty records; Expedia hasn't confirmed those figures.

items.head: Amadeus breach exposes data from at least five airlines' passengers
items.text: Unauthorized access to the airline booking provider ran from August 2023 to September 2026. Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, ANA, Korean Air and Condor are affected. Watch for phishing emails posing as your airline.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: The EU says the permit is not operational and has no launch date. Over 150 look-alike sites charge €50 to €178; the official fee will be €20.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Use Mobile Passport Control when flying home to DFW or Houston
items.text: US citizens can submit passport details and customs answers in a free app, then show a QR receipt to the CBP officer. Both DFW and IAH take part.

items.head: Hilton: up to 3,000 bonus points per stay
items.text: 3,000 points at resort and upscale hotels, 1,000 elsewhere, on cash or points stays. Register before your first stay.

items.head: AmaWaterways: up to $2,500 off per stateroom
items.text: On select 2026 and 2027 river sailings, with free upgrades on some cruises.

items.date: Car rental · pick up by Dec 31
items.head: Hertz: fifth day free on SUV and minivan rentals
items.text: Use promo code 212109 on 4- to 27-day SUV or minivan rentals picked up by December 31 to get the fifth day free.

items.head: Wyndham Rewards: 4x points
items.text: Book by January 15, 2027 and complete stays by January 19 to earn four times the usual Wyndham Rewards points.

items.head: IHG Black Friday: up to 30% off for members
items.text: IHG One Rewards members save up to 30% and nonmembers up to 20% on stays from November 21 through April 30, 2027.

items.head: Marriott Bonvoy: up to 25% off in the app
items.text: Members get up to 25% off through the mobile app, and anyone gets 15% on the website, for stays from November 29 to May 2, 2027.

items.head: Preferred Hotels: 35% off stays of two nights or more
items.text: The Black Friday sale covers Preferred Hotels properties, including Beyond Green, for stays through June 30, 2027.
